politicalLeanings.name: Far left
politicalLeanings.description: A position at the left extreme of the political spectrum, favoring radical economic redistribution and systemic change, often through anti-capitalist or revolutionary politics.

politicalLeanings.name: Left
politicalLeanings.description: A position on the left of the political spectrum, favoring social equality, expanded government programs and progressive social policy.

politicalLeanings.name: Center left
politicalLeanings.description: A moderate position left of center, supporting liberal social and economic policies while staying close to the political mainstream.

politicalLeanings.name: Center
politicalLeanings.description: A position near the middle of the political spectrum, balancing left and right perspectives without a consistent ideological tilt.

politicalLeanings.name: Center right
politicalLeanings.description: A moderate position right of center, supporting conservative social and economic policies while staying close to the political mainstream.

politicalLeanings.name: Right
politicalLeanings.description: A position on the right of the political spectrum, favoring limited government, free markets, traditional values and strong national defense.

politicalLeanings.name: Far right
politicalLeanings.description: A position at the right extreme of the political spectrum, marked by ultranationalism, nativism and hostility to pluralist institutions.

politicalLeanings.name: Nonpartisan
politicalLeanings.note: For entities that claim no side (wire services, fact-checkers, courts). Off the 1-7 scale.

ideologies.name: Decelerationist
ideologies.description: Informal label for a stance favoring slower technological development or deployment, especially of AI, to address perceived risks. The label has no single standardized policy program.

ideologies.name: Pro-online safety
ideologies.description: Supports measures to reduce harms associated with online services, such as abuse, exploitation, or harmful platform design. Specific approaches to moderation, privacy, and age verification vary.

ideologies.name: Pro-deregulation
ideologies.description: Favors reducing or simplifying government rules on businesses and markets.

ideologies.name: Pro-regulation
ideologies.description: Favors government rules and oversight to address market failures, protect the public, or constrain harmful conduct.

ideologies.name: Pro-court reform
ideologies.description: Supports changes to courts' structure, procedures, appointments, or ethics rules. Support for reform does not by itself specify a particular proposal or constitutional interpretation.

ideologies.name: Pro-criminal justice reform
ideologies.description: Supports changes to policing, courts, sentencing, or incarceration intended to improve fairness or outcomes.

ideologies.name: Pro-school choice
ideologies.description: Supports families having options beyond their assigned public school, including other public schools, charter schools, private schools, or homeschooling; funding preferences vary.

ideologies.name: Dove
ideologies.description: Favors restraint in using military force and prefers diplomacy or limited commitments.

ideologies.name: Pro-Iran containment
ideologies.description: Favors limiting Iran’s regional influence through deterrence, sanctions, or other pressure.

ideologies.name: Free trader
ideologies.description: Favors reducing barriers to international trade and maintaining open trade relationships.

ideologies.name: Pro-welfare expansion
ideologies.description: Supports expanding public benefits or social programs that provide income, health, or other assistance.

ideologies.name: Crypto skeptic
ideologies.description: Questions the benefits or safety of cryptocurrencies and favors caution or stronger safeguards.

ideologies.name: Pro-market wages
ideologies.description: Favors wages being determined primarily through labor-market bargaining rather than statutory wage floors or government-mandated increases.

ideologies.name: Pro-judicial independence
ideologies.description: Supports courts and judges deciding cases impartially, free from improper interference or pressure. Judicial independence can coexist with court reform and accountability.

ideologies.name: Pro-Taiwan defense
ideologies.description: Supports military assistance, deterrence, or defensive commitments intended to protect Taiwan against attack or coercion. This does not by itself imply support for a formal declaration of independence.

ideologies.name: Gender-critical
ideologies.description: Holds that biological sex is distinct from gender identity and should remain a basis for relevant legal and social distinctions. Specific policy positions vary.

ideologies.name: NATO skeptic
ideologies.description: Questions NATO’s purpose, costs, expansion, or members’ obligations.

ideologies.name: Climate skeptic
ideologies.description: Umbrella label for views questioning aspects of climate-change science, projected impacts, or proposed responses. Skepticism about a particular policy does not necessarily imply rejection of human-caused warming.

ideologies.name: Pro-LGBTQ rights
ideologies.description: Supports equal legal rights and protections for LGBTQ people.

ideologies.name: Pro-vaccination
ideologies.description: Supports vaccination as a means of preventing disease and protecting health. Support for vaccination does not by itself imply support for vaccine mandates.

ideologies.name: Pro-NATO
ideologies.description: Supports the North Atlantic Treaty Organization and its role in collective defense and security cooperation among its members.

ideologies.name: Pro-legalization
ideologies.description: Supports making specified currently prohibited drugs or related activities lawful under a legal framework. Legalization is distinct from only removing criminal penalties for possession or use.

ideologies.name: Church-state separationist
ideologies.description: Supports keeping government institutions and religious institutions legally separate.

ideologies.name: Protectionist
ideologies.description: Supports trade barriers or domestic preferences intended to protect local industries and workers from foreign competition.

ideologies.name: Pro-living wage
ideologies.description: Supports pay sufficient to afford a decent standard of living for workers and their families. This can be pursued through wage-setting policies, collective bargaining, or employer practices.

ideologies.name: Pro-foreign aid
ideologies.description: Supports providing assistance to other countries for purposes such as humanitarian relief, development, or security. Support is not limited to one agency or aid program.

ideologies.name: Pro-AI acceleration
ideologies.description: Supports faster development and deployment of artificial intelligence. Views on appropriate safety measures and regulation vary.

ideologies.name: Pro-Palestinian
ideologies.description: Supports Palestinian rights, interests, or political self-determination.

ideologies.name: Neighborhood preservation
ideologies.description: Favors protecting the character or stability of existing residential neighborhoods, often through local land-use controls.

ideologies.name: Pro-nuclear power
ideologies.description: Supports using or expanding nuclear energy to generate electricity.

ideologies.name: Progressive taxation
ideologies.description: Supports tax structures in which higher-income taxpayers pay a larger proportion of their income in tax than lower-income taxpayers.

ideologies.name: Pro-welfare reform
ideologies.description: Supports changes to public assistance programs' design, eligibility, administration, or incentives. The label alone does not establish whether benefits would expand or contract.

ideologies.name: Pro-immigration
ideologies.description: Supports immigration or policies that make immigration and immigrant integration easier.

ideologies.name: Pro-Ukraine
ideologies.description: Supports Ukraine’s sovereignty and its defense against Russia’s invasion.

ideologies.name: Pro-entitlement reform
ideologies.description: Supports changes to statutory benefit programs, such as Social Security or Medicare, to alter their financing, eligibility, or benefits. Proposals may expand or reduce particular benefits.

ideologies.name: Pro-repayment
ideologies.description: Favors borrowers repaying student loans and opposes or limits loan cancellation.

ideologies.name: Pro-public spending
ideologies.description: Supports government spending on public programs, services, or investment.

ideologies.name: Pro-Israel
ideologies.description: Supports Israel's security, national interests, or continued existence as a Jewish state. The label does not necessarily imply support for every Israeli government policy.

ideologies.name: Pro-election integrity
ideologies.description: Supports measures intended to ensure elections are accurate, secure, lawful, and fairly administered. Specific measures and their effects on voting access are matters of debate.

ideologies.name: Anti-nuclear
ideologies.description: Opposes nuclear power or its expansion.

ideologies.name: Pro-gun control
ideologies.description: Supports laws that restrict or regulate access to firearms.

ideologies.name: Pro-gun rights
ideologies.description: Supports legal protections for firearm ownership and use. Views on which restrictions are acceptable vary.

ideologies.name: Pro-internet freedom
ideologies.description: Supports freedom of expression, access to information, and participation online, with limits on censorship and unjustified restrictions.

ideologies.name: Pro-climate action
ideologies.description: Supports public or private measures to reduce climate change or adapt to its effects.

ideologies.name: Pro-states' rights
ideologies.description: Supports state governments’ authority relative to the federal government.

ideologies.name: Pro-fossil fuels
ideologies.description: Supports continued or expanded production and use of fossil fuels, including coal, oil, and natural gas.

ideologies.name: Social conservative
ideologies.description: Political outlook favoring traditional social institutions and moral norms, especially concerning family, religion, sexuality, and gender.

ideologies.name: Pro-universal healthcare
ideologies.description: Supports ensuring that everyone can obtain needed health services without financial hardship. Universal coverage can involve public, private, or mixed systems.

ideologies.name: Pro-innovation
ideologies.description: Supports policies or practices that encourage the development and adoption of new ideas, technologies, products, or processes.

ideologies.name: Pro-China engagement
ideologies.description: Supports diplomacy, trade, or cooperation with China rather than isolating or confronting it.

ideologies.name: Pro-voting rights
ideologies.description: Supports protecting or expanding access to voting and participation in elections.

ideologies.name: Fiscal hawk
ideologies.description: Favors limiting deficits and public debt through spending discipline, revenue, or both.

ideologies.name: Pro-federal authority
ideologies.description: Supports federal government authority over states in areas assigned to or best handled by the national government.

ideologies.name: Pro-border security
ideologies.description: Supports stronger enforcement and security measures at national borders.

ideologies.name: Pro-Iran diplomacy
ideologies.description: Supports negotiating with Iran and using diplomacy to manage disputes or reduce conflict.

ideologies.name: Pro-law enforcement
ideologies.description: Supports police and other law-enforcement agencies, their capacity, or their role in public safety.

ideologies.name: Pro-vaccine choice
ideologies.description: Supports individual choice about vaccination and opposes vaccine mandates.

ideologies.name: Pro-clean energy
ideologies.description: Supports energy sources with lower greenhouse-gas emissions, such as renewables or nuclear power.

ideologies.name: Pro-meritocracy
ideologies.description: Supports allocating opportunities, responsibilities, or rewards according to relevant ability, effort, and achievement. Views on how merit should be measured and unequal starting conditions addressed vary.

ideologies.name: Pro-equity
ideologies.description: Supports addressing unjust disadvantages and barriers to fair treatment or opportunities. The term's application to resources, procedures, and outcomes varies by context.

ideologies.name: Pro-religious freedom
ideologies.description: Supports the right to practice religion and protections for religious belief and exercise.

ideologies.name: Pro-housing development
ideologies.description: Supports building more housing or reducing barriers to new residential construction.

ideologies.name: Pro-foreign aid reform
ideologies.description: Supports changes to foreign assistance programs' objectives, allocation, delivery, or oversight. Reform may involve expansion, reduction, or redirection of particular programs.

ideologies.name: Pro-death penalty
ideologies.description: Supports retaining or applying capital punishment for certain serious crimes.

ideologies.name: Benefit preservation
ideologies.description: Supports maintaining existing public benefits or protecting recipients against benefit reductions, including in programs such as Social Security.

ideologies.name: Ukraine aid skeptic
ideologies.description: Questions the scale, duration, effectiveness, or conditions of assistance to Ukraine and may favor limiting or conditioning it. This stance does not by itself establish support for Russia.

ideologies.name: Prohibitionist
ideologies.description: In this dataset's drug-policy context, supports legal prohibitions on specified drugs or drug-related activities and opposes their legalization.

ideologies.name: Pro-tax cuts
ideologies.description: Supports reducing tax rates or the amount of tax people or businesses pay.
ideologies.slogan: Read my lips: no new taxes

ideologies.name: Pro-surveillance
ideologies.description: Supports using or expanding surveillance powers for purposes such as intelligence gathering, law enforcement, or security. Views on authorization, oversight, and privacy safeguards vary.

ideologies.name: Pro-transgender rights
ideologies.description: Supports equal legal rights and protections for transgender people.

ideologies.name: Pro-life
ideologies.description: Opposes abortion, especially on the grounds that fetal life should receive legal protection.

ideologies.name: Death penalty abolitionist
ideologies.description: Supports ending capital punishment.

ideologies.name: Pro-choice
ideologies.description: Supports legal access to abortion and the right to decide whether to continue a pregnancy.

ideologies.name: Pro-union
ideologies.description: Supports labor unions and collective bargaining rights for workers.

ideologies.name: Pro-public education
ideologies.description: Supports public schools and public investment in education.

ideologies.name: Hawk
ideologies.description: Favors a more forceful foreign policy and is comparatively willing to use military power.

ideologies.name: Pro-Taiwan restraint
ideologies.description: Favors limiting U.S. military commitments or escalation risks concerning Taiwan and prioritizing diplomacy or other nonmilitary approaches. This does not by itself imply support for unification with China.

ideologies.name: Pro-China containment
ideologies.description: Favors limiting China’s power or influence through deterrence, alliances, or other pressure.

ideologies.name: Pro-privacy
ideologies.description: Supports protecting personal information and limiting unwarranted data collection or surveillance.

ideologies.name: Anti-union
ideologies.description: Opposes labor unions or supports restricting their power, membership, or collective bargaining.

ideologies.name: Free-market healthcare
ideologies.description: Supports a greater role for market competition, private provision, and consumer choice in healthcare. Specific views on public financing, regulation, and assistance vary.

ideologies.name: Pro-crypto
ideologies.description: Supports cryptocurrencies and policies that enable their use or growth.

ideologies.name: Pro-AI regulation
ideologies.description: Supports rules or oversight governing the development or use of artificial intelligence.

ideologies.name: Pro-student debt relief
ideologies.description: Supports reducing or cancelling student loan debt for borrowers.

ideologies.name: Techno-optimist
ideologies.description: Broad outlook expecting technological development to produce substantial benefits for human well-being. It does not by itself imply support for every technology or for removing all regulation.

ideologies.name: Anti-Zionist
ideologies.description: Opposes Zionism as a political ideology or movement supporting Jewish national self-determination in Israel. Anti-Zionist positions vary and extend beyond criticism of particular Israeli government policies.

ideologies.name: Classical liberal
ideologies.description: Political philosophy emphasizing individual liberty, civil liberties, private property, the rule of law, and limits on government power; views on the state's economic role vary.

ideologies.name: Nationalist
ideologies.description: Political outlook that gives special importance to national identity and self-government and prioritizes the nation's interests. Nationalist traditions differ on citizenship, ethnicity, and international cooperation.

ideologies.name: Globalist
ideologies.description: Political outlook favoring international integration and cooperation in economic and foreign affairs. The label has several meanings and is also used pejoratively.

ideologies.name: Secularist
ideologies.description: Political outlook favoring state neutrality toward religion and belief and limits on religious authority over government. Secularism does not require individuals to be nonreligious.

ideologies.name: Conservative
ideologies.description: Political tradition valuing inherited institutions, customs, and social continuity and generally favoring cautious change. Its policies and understanding of tradition vary across countries and periods.

ideologies.name: Paleoconservative
ideologies.description: A U.S. conservative current emphasizing national sovereignty, cultural tradition, restrictive immigration, and restraint in foreign intervention.

ideologies.name: MAGA
ideologies.description: Political movement and associated nationalist-populist outlook centered on Donald Trump's Make America Great Again slogan, emphasizing America First policies, immigration restrictions, and opposition to political elites.

ideologies.name: Democratic socialist
ideologies.description: Socialist outlook combining political democracy with social ownership and democratic control of economic life. It is distinct from policies that solely regulate capitalism or expand welfare.

ideologies.name: Liberal
ideologies.description: In contemporary U.S. politics, an outlook supporting civil liberties, equal rights, and government action to address social and economic inequalities. Liberalism has broader and differing meanings internationally.

ideologies.name: Socialist
ideologies.description: Family of political and economic views favoring social ownership or democratic control of productive resources rather than their predominantly private ownership. Socialist traditions differ on markets, planning, and political strategy.

ideologies.name: Feminist
ideologies.description: Family of social and political perspectives seeking equality for women and challenging sex- and gender-based subordination. Feminist traditions differ in their explanations of inequality and proposed remedies.

ideologies.name: Marxist
ideologies.description: Social and political outlook drawing on Karl Marx's analysis of class relations, historical change, and capitalism, including its critique of exploitation and class domination.

ideologies.name: Neoconservative
ideologies.description: A conservative outlook associated with an assertive U.S. foreign policy, military strength, and support for promoting democracy abroad.

ideologies.name: Communist
ideologies.description: Political ideology seeking a classless society based on common ownership of productive resources. Communist traditions differ over how to achieve that goal and the role of the state.

ideologies.name: Social democrat
ideologies.description: In its contemporary sense, a political tradition supporting a predominantly market economy alongside democratic government, economic regulation, labor protections, and extensive public services and social welfare.

ideologies.name: Humanist
ideologies.description: Ethical and philosophical worldview emphasizing human dignity, reason, and human welfare. Broader than a specifically political ideology, humanism includes both religious and nonreligious traditions.

ideologies.name: Traditionalist
ideologies.description: An outlook that values inherited customs and institutions and favors preserving social continuity over rapid change.

ideologies.name: Neoliberal
ideologies.description: Contested label for political and economic ideas emphasizing markets, private enterprise, and competition, often associated with privatization, deregulation, and trade liberalization; views on welfare and state institutions vary.

ideologies.name: Populist
ideologies.description: Political outlook presenting society as divided between the people and a corrupt elite and demanding that politics express the people's will. It can combine with left-wing or right-wing ideologies.

ideologies.name: Libertarian
ideologies.description: Political outlook giving individual liberty priority and opposing coercive interference. In contemporary U.S. usage, it commonly combines strong private-property rights and market freedom with civil liberties.

ideologies.name: Islamist
ideologies.description: Family of political outlooks seeking to organize government and public life according to interpretations of Islamic principles. Islamist movements differ substantially and should not be equated with Islam or Muslim identity.

ideologies.name: Environmentalist
ideologies.description: Broad social and political outlook placing protection of the natural environment at the center of public concerns, including conservation, pollution prevention, and ecological sustainability.

ideologies.name: Progressive
ideologies.description: A U.S. political outlook supporting reforms or structural changes to expand social and economic equality, civil rights, and environmental protection.

ideologies.name: Libertarianism
ideologies.description: A political philosophy that prioritizes individual liberty and limits state power in economic and personal affairs. Libertarian traditions differ on the proper scope of government.

ideologies.name: Christian conservative
ideologies.description: Conservative political outlook informed by Christian beliefs and moral traditions, often emphasizing religion's public role and traditional views on family, marriage, and abortion.

ideologies.name: Isolationist
ideologies.description: Foreign-policy outlook favoring avoidance of foreign wars and binding political or military commitments. It is distinct from simply opposing one intervention and need not mean ending all international trade.

ideologies.name: Anarchist
ideologies.description: A political outlook opposing the state and other coercive hierarchies and favoring voluntary association and self-governance. Anarchist traditions differ widely on property, markets, and social organization.
